title: Risk Calibrator and Cohort Prefetch Rollout Playbook
creator: Asha Patel
summary: Automate batching/caching recommendations and stage safe config apply with cohort-based prefetch and anomaly-driven rollback to protect latency/throughput SLOs while reducing unit cost.
description:
Problem: Teams need automated suggestions for batching and KV-prefetch configurations to reduce token costs, but naive bulk rollout causes regression in latency p95/p99 and throughput. This ticket implements a Risk Calibrator service and a staged Cohort Prefetch Rollout Playbook that applies recommendations with limiters, SLO-aware routing, and anomaly detection to ensure safe economic wins.

Scope:
- A Decision Engine that produces recommended batching (batch size, microwindow, max latency) and caching profiles (prefix levels, TTL heuristics) per model-route cohort.
- A Rollout Orchestrator that: 1) applies changes to shadow cohorts, 2) executes micro-canaries with traffic shaping, 3) observes SLO and cost signals, and 4) triggers automatic rollback on anomalies.
- Runtime guardrails: limiter primitives (token-budget guards, inflight-request caps, adaptive backpressure), SLO-aware routing (route to stable variant when latency risk detected), and anomaly detection (multi-signal scoring + hysteresis).

Non-goals: full UI surface for recommendations (console work will follow in a separate ticket), model retraining, or global autoscaling policy changes outside of rollout cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Decision Engine generates per-route recommendation artifacts (JSON) with batching and caching parameters and a confidence score.
Rollout Orchestrator can create shadow cohorts and run 0%->1%->10%->50% staged canaries with configurable ramp steps.

Automatic rollback triggers if p95 latency increases by >15% or p99 increases by >10% sustained for 5 minutes, or error rate rises by >0.5 percentage points, or cost per token deviates by >20% from expected.
SLO-aware router can divert new requests to pinned stable model variant or a higher-tier routing path when cohort signals cross thresholds.
Anomaly detector raises an alert and creates a dashboard snapshot link when a rollback occurs; rollback is completed automatically and recorded in audit logs.
Non-regression tests: synthetic replay harness proves no >5% throughput regression for 95% of routes under median production-like load in staging cluster.

2025-03-01: Tuned limiter: added inflight_request cap per-worker and token_budget per-request to prevent overload of sparse-serving models under aggressive batching.

Next steps: run systematic synthetic-replay across 200 representative routes, add ML-based anomaly scorer to reduce false positives, implement console visibility card.
notes: Decision trade-offs: conservative confidence threshold (0.65) reduces candidate pool to avoid noisy low-data routes, but may miss some cost wins. We can relax threshold after 90-day safe window.
Testing strategy: shadow -> 1% canary -> 10% canary -> 50% ramp with manual gate before 100%. All ramps have automatic timers and rollback predicates.
Rollout economics: aim for net unit-cost reduction >= 8% per-route; flag routes with <3% expected savings as 'no-op' to avoid churn.
Observability: dashboards must show cohort delta (latency, errors, cost), and a compact histogram of token distribution to interpret batching behavior.
Failure modes: aggressive prefetch can increase on-device memory and KV overhead causing throughput loss; limiter primitives must cap memory footprint per-worker.
